Houston Cougars.previous_hc_experience: Yes. The guide records Willie Fritz winning everywhere, singles out his success at Tulane, and notes he went 4-8 in year one at Houston and 10-3 in year two.
Houston Cougars.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Houston Cougars.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Houston Cougars.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Houston Cougars.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records Houston tying for 41st nationally in Adjusted EPA per play allowed at -0.05 and allowing 22.8 points per game.
Houston Cougars.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Houston Cougars.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide's quarterback material is a deployment question — whether Fritz can afford to keep five-star Keisean Henderson on the bench all season behind Conner Weigman, reasoning that elite quarterback play could make Houston a legitimate national title contender.
Houston Cougars.continuity: Complete. The Stability Score table (p. 42) awards points for a returning head coach, offensive coordinator, defensive coordinator and quarterback — 4, 3, 3 and 4, plus 4 for 19 returning starters — totalling 18, the highest recorded in this batch.
Houston Cougars.staff_turnover: Not addressed in guide. The Stability Score table records both coordinators returning.
Houston Cougars.prior_school: Tulane, and the connection is on the roster too: the guide records Makhi Hughes reuniting with Fritz after running for 1,401 yards and 15 touchdowns there in 2024, arguing he has thrived in this system before. Other additions recorded are Ashton Porter, De'Marion Thomas and Jordan Allen.
Houston Cougars.portal_recruiting: Tied to the coach's own history — the guide's central portal argument is the Fritz-Hughes reunion, framing the back as the head of the snake in a system he already knows.
Houston Cougars.vsin_assessment: Unreservedly positive on the coach. The guide says Fritz has won everywhere, treats his momentum at Houston as unsurprising, calls the programme a long-time sleeping giant and Fritz the perfect hire to get it over the hump, and calls this year-three roster arguably the most talented he has ever coached — which it notes is significant given his success at Tulane. Playoff qualification is on the table.
Houston Cougars.strengths: A Stability Score of 18 with everything returning, 19 returning starters, a head coach the guide calls the perfect hire with a documented year-on-year jump, nine returning defensive starters with coordinator Austin Armstrong credited with the talent, size and depth, and a five-star quarterback in reserve.
Houston Cougars.concerns: A starting quarterback the guide calls a little inefficient as a passer at a 63.5 PFF throwing grade who struggled badly in some of Houston's biggest games, and a defense that needs both a rise in pass-rush production and steadier secondary play to reach its stated goal.
Houston Cougars.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.

Iowa State Cyclones.previous_hc_experience: Extensive for his age, and the Coaching Carousel sets it out precisely: Jimmy Rogers won the FCS National Championship in his first season as a head coach at South Dakota State and lost in the semifinal in year two, and this will be just his third year at the FBS level, having served as a GA at Florida Atlantic in 2012 under Carl Pelini and then as head coach of Washington State last season.
Iowa State Cyclones.dc: Jesse Bobbit, brought from Washington State.
Iowa State Cyclones.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Iowa State Cyclones.dc_status: New — the guide records Rogers bringing Bobbit with him, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Iowa State Cyclones.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Iowa State Cyclones.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Iowa State Cyclones.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme. The guide records Bobbit running a top-50 unit by Adjusted EPA per play allowed at -0.05, with only 25 teams allowing fewer points than Washington State's 20.2.
Iowa State Cyclones.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide calls Jaylen Raynor exciting and a fun dual-threat for Arkansas State while saying he turns the ball over too often and that little suggests he can carve up Big 12 defenses.
Iowa State Cyclones.continuity: None. The Stability Score table (p. 42) prints 0 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator, 0 for the quarterback and 0 for 4 returning starters — a total of 0, the lowest score in the guide.
Iowa State Cyclones.staff_turnover: Complete. Matt Campbell left for Penn State taking 11 assistants with him, and Rogers arrived with his own coordinator from Washington State.
Iowa State Cyclones.prior_school: Washington State, for both the coordinator and key players — the guide records the Cyclones importing key Washington State pieces plus notable contributors from smaller programmes. South Dakota State is where Rogers won his championship. On the offensive line it records Braden Smith from Tarleton State, Caden Mass from Sioux Falls, Colin Amick from Montana and Jake Taylor from Oklahoma.
Iowa State Cyclones.portal_recruiting: Central to the rebuild and described as such: Rogers hit the portal extremely hard for a mix of high-major players needing opportunity and successful lower-level players wanting a bigger stage.
Iowa State Cyclones.vsin_assessment: Benefit of the doubt from both places the guide addresses it, with the timeline set beyond this season. The Coaching Carousel says time will tell whether this is a good hire, notes AD Jamie Pollard has made good ones before, records the $4 million buyout paid to free Rogers from Washington State as evidence Pollard was locked in from the jump, says Pollard unequivocally deserves the benefit of the doubt, and adds that Rogers inherits a much better foundation than his predecessor did from Paul Rhoads. The team pages are careful not to write him off — ruling out Rogers turning Iowa State into a winner would be foolish because good coaches win in Ames — while judging it may take more than a season.
Iowa State Cyclones.strengths: An FCS national title in a first head-coaching season and an FBS season already behind him at 39, a defensive coordinator whose Washington State unit the guide calls elite, an athletic department that paid $4 million to secure him, a much better inherited foundation than his predecessor had, and a defense the guide expects to be in a very good place.
Iowa State Cyclones.concerns: A Stability Score of 0 with only four returning starters, an offensive line rebuilt from Tarleton State, Sioux Falls, Montana and an Oklahoma player who missed all of last season, a quarterback who turns the ball over too often, no proven pass catchers and a shaky running back group — the guide states as a real possibility that this could be the worst offense in the Big 12.
Iowa State Cyclones.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument.
Iowa State Cyclones.carousel_summary: Adam Burke frames the hire through the athletic director: time will tell whether or not this is a good hire, but AD Jamie Pollard has made some good ones with Matt Campbell on the football side and Fred Hoiberg, Steve Prohm and T.J. Otzelberger on the basketball side. He records the commitment in money — $4 million to buy Rogers out of his Washington State contract, so Pollard was locked in from the jump on the 39-year-old — and the record behind it: an FCS National Championship in his first season as a head coach at South Dakota State and a semifinal loss in year two. He is explicit that this will be just Rogers' third year at the FBS level, having served as a GA at Florida Atlantic in 2012 under Carl Pelini and then as head coach of Washington State last season. His conclusion is that Pollard unequivocally deserves the benefit of the doubt here, and that Rogers inherits a much better foundation than his predecessor did from Paul Rhoads.

Kansas Jayhawks.oc: Andy Kotelnicki, a former Broyles Award nominee, returning after an up-and-down spell at Penn State.
Kansas Jayhawks.oc_status: The guide states this two ways — see the conflicts field. The team pages (pp. 132–133) treat Kotelnicki's return as news and say it means Kansas will run the most successful offense it has used in decades, while the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Kansas Jayhawks.dc_status: The guide states this two ways — see the conflicts field. The team pages call DK McDonald the new coordinator, while the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Kansas Jayhawks.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Kansas Jayhawks.offensive_scheme: Named. The guide describes Kotelnicki's pro-style system as using heavy pre-snap motion to create mismatches, and stresses that none of it works without an efficient, physical run game.
Kansas Jayhawks.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Kansas Jayhawks.run_pass: Stated as dependent on the run: the guide says line play is critical because the pro-style motion system needs an efficient, physical run game, especially with quarterback uncertainty.
Kansas Jayhawks.personnel: Addressed through the heavy pre-snap motion the scheme uses.
Kansas Jayhawks.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide says the quarterback situation looks ugly with Jalon Daniels gone and concludes Kotelnicki may not produce an elite offense immediately.
Kansas Jayhawks.continuity: Head coach returns and both coordinator columns print returning points, but the quarterback changes. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 4, 3, 3 and 0, plus 2 for 12 returning starters, totalling 12. The team pages describe both coordinator positions differently — see the conflicts field.
Kansas Jayhawks.staff_turnover: The team pages record two coordinator moves: Kotelnicki returning from Penn State, and DK McDonald taking over the defense.
Kansas Jayhawks.prior_school: Penn State, twice over — Kotelnicki went to Happy Valley when James Franklin took him there, a move the guide says ultimately worked out for no one, and has now come back.
Kansas Jayhawks.portal_recruiting: Addressed as defensive repair. The guide expects some improvement after portal work, and records impressive bodies added to the offensive line.
Kansas Jayhawks.vsin_assessment: A rise, a stall, and a warm seat. The guide records Lance Leipold looking set to become a Lawrence legend, taking Kansas from 2-10 to 6-7 to 9-4 in 2023 and helping secure serious financial investment from the university, then says back-to-back 5-7 seasons have left him with an uncomfortably warm seat. It calls Kotelnicki's return good news — meaning Kansas will run the most successful offense it has used in decades, having averaged 35.6 and 34.8 points per game in 2022 and 2023 — while stating clearly that the pieces are not in place right now. It closes by noting that if things go extremely poorly, Leipold's situation becomes interesting.
Kansas Jayhawks.strengths: A head coach with a documented three-year turnaround and institutional investment behind him, the return of a Broyles Award nominee whose Kansas offenses were among the most potent in the country, real potential for one of the better Big 12 offensive lines with a future pro at left tackle, and portal work the guide expects to improve the defense somewhat.
Kansas Jayhawks.concerns: Two straight 5-7 seasons, a quarterback room the guide calls ugly after losing one of the sport's best dual threats, a receiver room it says appears to lack game-changing talent, and a defense that allowed 26.8 points per game and could not crack the top 100 in Adjusted EPA per play allowed.
Kansas Jayhawks.betting: Recommendation is Under 5.5 wins. Without Jalon Daniels' playmaking to mask deficiencies the guide expects a tough year, says this is not a team to trust in 50-50 games given the quarterback options and a mediocre defense, and notes that if things go extremely poorly Leipold's situation becomes interesting.
Kansas Jayhawks.conflicts: The guide states both coordinator positions two ways. The team pages (pp. 132–133) present Andy Kotelnicki's return from Penn State as a change and call DK McDonald the new defensive coordinator, while the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator and 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator. All are reproduced as printed and none is corrected.

Kansas State Wildcats.previous_hc_experience: None as a head coach. The Coaching Carousel records that Collin Klein was on the Kansas State staff in 2014-15 and again from 2017-23, serving primarily as quarterbacks coach and then offensive coordinator, before two seasons at Texas A&M. The team pages state plainly that this is his first time running an entire programme, so a seamless transition is not guaranteed.
Kansas State Wildcats.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Kansas State Wildcats.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Kansas State Wildcats.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name. The guide's related observation is that receivers must create space when Klein is not scheming them open.
Kansas State Wildcats.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Kansas State Wildcats.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme.
Kansas State Wildcats.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split.
Kansas State Wildcats.qb_development: Framed as a scheme-fit expectation. The guide argues there should be another gear in Avery Johnson — he is among the nation's most impressive athletes at the position and Klein's return should mean a perfect scheme fit — while asking directly whether 2025's flat numbers are simply who he is, and separately saying it is not sold on Klein instantly fixing the offense.
Kansas State Wildcats.continuity: Broken across the staff, intact at quarterback. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 0 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator and 4 for the quarterback, plus 2 for 12 returning starters, totalling 6.
Kansas State Wildcats.staff_turnover: Complete at the top. The guide records Chris Klieman stepping down after a 6-6 season citing family and personal health, credits him with at least nine wins in three consecutive years before that and with succeeding the legendary Bill Snyder well, and describes the incoming group as a young staff.
Kansas State Wildcats.prior_school: Texas A&M, where Klein spent two seasons — and the connection reaches the roster, with the guide offering Izaiah Williams, who followed Klein from Texas A&M, as a possible breakout and the missing piece. Kansas State itself is the deeper connection: Klein played there from 2008 to 2012 and coached there across two spells.
Kansas State Wildcats.portal_recruiting: Defensive-front focused. The guide records Oklahoma State transfer Wendell Gregory, Cincinnati transfer Kamari Burns and Kentucky transfer Austin Ramsey plus productive linebackers, while cautioning that bringing in an entirely new crop is difficult.
Kansas State Wildcats.vsin_assessment: Positive on the man, cautious about the staff's collective inexperience. The Coaching Carousel calls Klein one of the best players in the programme's history, says he does seem to be a solid coach given that he is only 36 and already has this job after Chris Klieman and Bill Snyder — two men it says excelled in Manhattan for boosters and bettors — then identifies the risk: with OC Sean Gleeson and DC Jordan Peterson this is a young staff that will learn and grow together, so bumps in the road are inevitable, and this was just a 6-6 programme last season. The team pages call Klein a brilliant offensive mind at his destination job while stating this is his first time running a whole programme.
Kansas State Wildcats.strengths: A head coach the guide calls a brilliant offensive mind in his destination job with deep programme roots, a returning electric dual-threat quarterback the guide says should fit his scheme perfectly, talent on both sides, a secondary combining talent and experience, and a coaching succession the guide credits as strong before him.
Kansas State Wildcats.concerns: A first-time head coach with a young coordinator pair the Carousel says will learn and grow together, making bumps in the road inevitable; 164.0 rushing yards per game allowed with an entirely new front to fix it; a quarterback the guide says must earn back lost trust; and a receiver group it calls mediocre after losing its deep threat to LSU.
Kansas State Wildcats.betting: Not addressed in guide as an explicit coaching-driven market argument. Its coaching-linked reservations are stated instead: it is not sold on Klein instantly fixing the offense, and it notes Kansas State can easily be tripped up by Houston, Kansas and Arizona in Manhattan.
Kansas State Wildcats.carousel_summary: Adam Burke's frame is homecoming and youth. After spreading his wings to fly to College Station for two seasons, Klein is back in the Little Apple to coach at his alma mater; he was on the staff in 2014-15 and again from 2017-23, serving primarily as the QB coach and then OC. Burke calls him one of the best players in the programme's history and says he does seem to be a solid coach, given that he is only 36 and already has this job after Chris Klieman and Bill Snyder, two men who excelled in Manhattan for boosters and bettors. His reservation is about the whole staff rather than the man: with OC Sean Gleeson and DC Jordan Peterson, this is a young staff that will learn and grow together, so bumps in the road are inevitable — and this was just a 6-6 programme last season.

Oklahoma State Cowboys.previous_hc_experience: Yes. The guide records Eric Morris leading North Texas to 12-2 last season — the programme's first AP ranking in over 65 years and a chance at being the Group of Five CFP representative — and notes he went 5-7 in his first year there. The Coaching Carousel adds that he played and coached under Mike Leach and Kliff Kingsbury.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.dc: Skyler Cassity, whom the Coaching Carousel calls an excellent DC.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.dc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.play_caller: Not addressed in guide by name.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.offensive_scheme: Named. The guide calls Morris another Air Raid coach bringing excitement, and records that North Texas had the most explosive offense in college football under him. The Coaching Carousel's phrase is that the gunslinger mentality is back in Stillwater.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.defensive_scheme: Not addressed as a named scheme, but a stated identity is recorded: Cassity was praised for turning the North Texas defense into a high-turnover unit and will hope the aggressive style works in the Big 12.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.tempo: Not addressed directly. The guide's characterisation of the offense is explosiveness rather than pace.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated split beyond the Air Raid label.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.qb_development: Addressed as continuity rather than development: Morris brought a group of his former players for year one, Drew Mestemaker among them, and the guide records Mestemaker as the best Group of Five quarterback in the country with the best numbers of any FBS quarterback.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.continuity: None. The Stability Score table (p. 43) prints 0 for the head coach, 0 for the offensive coordinator, 0 for the defensive coordinator and 0 for the quarterback, plus 2 for 10 returning starters, totalling 2.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.staff_turnover: Complete. The guide records longtime head coach Mike Gundy dismissed after a combined 4-11 across 2024 and 2025 — the Coaching Carousel puts the two-year record at 4-20 including 0-18 in the new-look Big 12 — and Morris arriving with his own staff and players.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.prior_school: North Texas, comprehensively — Morris, quarterback Drew Mestemaker, coordinator Skyler Cassity and a group of former players. On the offensive line the guide records second-team All-AAC guard Johnny Dickson, three Power Four starters and a starting guard from Coastal Carolina.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.portal_recruiting: The main rebuilding tool. Oklahoma State lost seven players from last year's offensive line options, so Morris went to the portal; the guide notes experience will not be lacking but leaves quality genuinely open, and frames this as one of the most important position groups in the country this year.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.vsin_assessment: A clean break credited to both sides. The guide expects a Mike Gundy statue in Stillwater eventually while judging plainly that the game passed him by — he had zero interest in adjusting to the new era. On the successor the Coaching Carousel is enthusiastic: a return to the glory days may not be that far away, the gunslinger mentality is back, and it thinks the Cowboys make a big leap, especially with an excellent DC in Skyler Cassity. The team pages temper that with precedent — the Big 12 makes a quick turnaround hard, and Morris himself went 5-7 in his first year at North Texas.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.strengths: A head coach with the most explosive offense in college football at his previous stop and a lineage under Mike Leach and Kliff Kingsbury, a defensive coordinator the Carousel calls excellent and credits with doing more with less, a transplanted quarterback who was the best in the Group of Five, and a portal offensive line the guide says will not lack experience.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.concerns: A Stability Score of 2, a quarterback with more interceptions than touchdowns in two of North Texas's biggest games, an offensive line rebuilt wholesale, and a defense with only four players who started in 2025 in the projected lineup — which the guide says could be one of the Big 12's worst and is why it is hard to fully buy Oklahoma State as a conference sleeper.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.betting: Recommendation is Over 5.5 wins. The coaching link is stated on both sides: the guide calls the defense's look concerning while crediting coordinator Skyler Cassity with doing more with less, and identifies the 12 September game against Oregon as the early test of the quarterback.
Oklahoma State Cowboys.carousel_summary: Adam Burke opens optimistically: a return to the glory days of Oklahoma State football may not be that far away. He measures the fall first — hard to believe this was a top-10 team in 2021 and a 10-win team in 2023, given how badly the last two seasons went, with the Cowboys a combined 4-20 and 0-18 in the new-look Big 12, prompting the pink slip for longtime head coach Mike Gundy. He then introduces Morris, who played and coached under Mike Leach and Kliff Kingsbury and led North Texas to the programme's first AP ranking in over 65 years and a chance at being the G5 CFP representative. His conclusion is direct: the gunslinger mentality is back in Stillwater, and he thinks the Cowboys make a big leap, especially with an excellent DC in Skyler Cassity.
